summary:
StellarVitals is a health monitoring web app designed to help astronauts keep track of their health during long space missions. It allows crew members to complete daily health check-ins, view their results, and understand how their bodies are changing over time. The dashboard tracks important health indicators, while the interactive body map explains how different organs and body systems are affected by spaceflight. Astronauts can also view health trends, learn about space-related health risks, and follow step-by-step instructions during emergencies.

We use NASA research and real NASA data sources to help explain spaceflight health risks and provide environmental information. The app also uses simulated astronaut readings to show how health changes can be tracked and flagged. By bringing health information, reminders, and emergency guidance into one place, StellarVitals helps astronauts make better-informed decisions, especially when communication with Earth is delayed. Our goal is to make long missions safer by helping astronauts understand their health and act when something changes.
details:
StellarVitals is a health monitoring website designed to help astronauts keep track of their health during long space missions. It turns daily health checks into a simple, guided process so crew members can understand their results and know when something might be wrong.

The website includes daily check-ins that guide astronauts through measurements like blood pressure, heart rate, temperature, sleep, and mood. Each step explains how to take the measurement and why it matters. The health dashboard brings everything together by showing four main risk areas: radiation, bone and muscle, heart and circulation, and behavioral health. It also displays a readiness score, stress-load count, and health indicators with status labels and trend lines.

StellarVitals also tracks health changes over time by comparing readings with each astronaut's personal baseline. Mission events, such as solar particle events or changes in cabin CO₂, can be shown alongside the trends to help explain possible changes. The interactive body map lets astronauts explore different body systems, understand how spaceflight hazards affect them, and learn about related health indicators and ways to prevent problems. For emergencies, the website provides step-by-step instructions for situations such as chest pain, includes timers, and creates a summary that can be shared with ground support. Different environment modes can also adjust reminders and alerts for the ISS, deep-space travel, the Moon, and Mars.

StellarVitals uses a set of rules to decide whether a health reading is OK, WATCH, or ACT NOW. It looks at set thresholds, each astronaut's personal baseline, recent trends, and combinations of symptoms and readings. For example, chest pain together with a high heart rate and abnormal blood pressure can trigger an emergency alert. Each alert explains why it was triggered. The main safety features work directly in the browser, so they do not need an internet connection. This is important because communication with Earth can take around 20 minutes each way from Mars.

Since real astronaut health records are private, the website uses simulated data from a 90-day mission with three fictional crew members and planned health events. Real NASA data is also used for space-weather alerts and an ISS radiation sample. NASA research and standards help guide the health indicators and scientific information used throughout the website.

During long space missions, astronauts may not be able to get immediate help from doctors on Earth. StellarVitals gives them a way to check their health, understand changes, and follow clear steps when something needs attention. The goal is to help astronauts make better-informed decisions and catch possible health problems earlier. The same idea could also be useful for remote clinics and communities on Earth that have limited access to healthcare

The tools used to build the project include React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, React Router, Phosphor Icons, Fira Sans, Overpass, Vitest, GitHub, and VS Code with AI coding assistants.
